item.title: Marc Andreessen is wrong about introspection
item.description:
📝 And he is entirely wrong about introspection. These are claims about what will make people's lives go well. But none, not one single of these measurements will tell you whether the people whose lives they describe feel that their lives are worth living, whether they find their work meaningful, whether they wake up with something that resembles purpose.
🔗 Read more: https://www.joanwestenberg.com/marc-andreessen-is-wrong-about-introspection/

item.title: Big-Endian Testing with QEMU
item.description:
📝 In computing, the terms big endian and little endian refer to the order in which a value's bytes are stored in memory: with the most significant (big) or least significant (little) part first. If we instruct a computer to store it at some memory address mem, the computer's endianness determines whether the least significant byte (0x78) or the most significant byte (0x12) gets stored at the first memory address, mem[0]. ) When programming, it is still important to write code that runs correctly on systems with either byte order (see for example The byte order fallacy).
🔗 Read more: https://www.hanshq.net/big-endian-qemu.html
